channel.title: AI Frontier Post
channel.description: Dispatches from the AI frontier: AI news, research explainers, frontier lab coverage, and product comparisons.

item.title: Strip the noise, keep the voice: hands-on with Inworld's Voice Isolator and SAVA
item.dc:creator: Sofia Almeida
item.description: Inworld open-sourced the voice-isolation and turn-taking models behind its realtime voice products. I installed both, ran them on the repo's own noisy sample, and measured it: silent gaps cut by ~50 dB, speech kept within a decibel, and a realtime twin that matches the offline model to 0.999 correlation.

item.title: See what your AI agent actually did: hands-on with Arize Phoenix observability
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: Three frontier agent models shipped in 48 hours. The question isn't whether you can build an agent — it's whether you can see what it did. This tutorial wires a local agent to Arize Phoenix, traces every call, and turns the results into evals and experiments — no API key, no cloud, no cost.

item.title: Inworld open-sources a voice isolator that pulls clean speech out of noisy recordings — live, in 20 milliseconds
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: Inworld’s Voice Isolator v1 is a small, Apache-2.0 open-weight model that strips crowd noise, music and room echo from speech — and a realtime twin does it live with 20 milliseconds of look-ahead. A 39-second demo on r/LocalLLaMA shows the before-and-after.

item.title: Red-team your own chatbot: hands-on with Microsoft's PyRIT
item.dc:creator: Sofia Almeida
item.description: Microsoft's AI red team open-sourced the toolkit it uses to break chatbots. Install PyRIT, point it at a local model, and run a real jailbreak scan — no API keys, no GPU, no cloud.

item.title: California pulls Waymo off its freeways — and Waymo pulls itself off every US highway
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: California’s DMV barred Waymo’s driverless cars from state freeways after repeated construction-zone incursions, calling the service an ‘imminent hazard’ to public safety. Waymo has now paused freeway rides nationwide.

item.title: Palo Alto Networks bets $4.5 billion on Applied Compute — and on securing open-weight AI
item.dc:creator: Priya Nair
item.description: Palo Alto Networks agreed to buy Applied Compute, an 18-month-old startup that trains and runs open-weight AI models, in a $4.5 billion all-stock deal announced alongside a record quarter.

item.title: Build a long-context research analyst with Gemini 4 Neon: thinking levels, structured output, and long decode, end to end
item.dc:creator: Sofia Almeida
item.description: Google's new mid-tier model costs $3/$15 per million tokens, thinks at four levels, and reads a million tokens of PDFs, charts, and spreadsheets in one call. This tutorial builds a complete research analyst on the Interactions API — verified call by call against the Python SDK — and prices every run to the cent.

item.title: Koharu’s local-first manga translator is now a full AI editor — layers, generative fill, and an MCP agent, all running on your machine
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: Two months of rebuilding turned the open-source Koharu manga translator into a Photoshop-style editor — layers, generative fill, and a proofreading agent — with every model still running on your own machine.

item.title: Google releases Gemini 4 Neon, the mid-tier model its billing catalog leaked this morning
item.dc:creator: Sofia Almeida
item.description: Hours after pricing for an unannounced Gemini 4 Neon surfaced in Google Cloud's billing catalog, Google made it official: the model is live in the API and AI Studio at $3 in and $15 out per million tokens, with a 1M-token context window and a model card to match.

item.title: Microsoft and Salesforce launch Copilotforce, bringing Salesforce CRM into Copilot
item.dc:creator: Sofia Almeida
item.description: Microsoft and Salesforce unveiled Copilotforce at Ignite: Salesforce’s CRM context and sales workflows inside Microsoft Copilot, with 38+ prebuilt sales skills in public preview and zero-copy links between Data 360 and Fabric.

item.title: GPT-6.2 Astra formalizes Smoktunowicz's Gap Theorem — the first Lean proof of the 2006 result, Vals AI says
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: Vals AI reports that GPT-6.2 Astra produced the first machine-checked proof of a 2006 algebra theorem — 1,794 lines of Lean in 94 minutes, after the model nearly gave up halfway through.

item.title: Make product promos with your coding agent: hands-on with video-shotcraft's 124-shot Remotion library
item.dc:creator: Priya Nair
item.description: video-shotcraft gives Claude Code and Codex a 124-card library of tuned camera moves, a complete 36-second promo template, and a browser workbench — every frame drawn by code from your own screenshots. This tutorial installs the skill, renders the template, and walks one shot card end to end, with every command verified.

item.title: Trump administration weighs forcing US firms to disclose their Chinese AI use
item.dc:creator: Priya Nair
item.description: The Treasury Department and the White House science office have discussed requiring companies like Airbnb to post their use of Chinese AI models on their websites — a ‘name and shame’ push that stops short of a ban.

item.title: Bank CEOs, NSA tell Congress: rushed patches for AI-found flaws caused this week's outages
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: Wall Street executives and the NSA told lawmakers the outages grounding flights, freezing bank accounts and degrading the NSA's network came not from a cyberattack but from a rush to patch vulnerabilities AI models had found — and the fixes overwhelmed systems built to be patched slowly.

item.title: Nvidia stops shipping H200 AI chips to China — ending the licensed channel Huang built
item.dc:creator: Sofia Almeida
item.description: Interim CEO Colette Kress told investors Nvidia is no longer shipping licensed Hopper chips to China, closing the arrangement Jensen Huang brokered with the White House — and a new US rule now reaches the overseas data centers that served Chinese customers from abroad.

item.title: Build a coding agent with GPT-6.2 Astra: apply_patch, shell, and the migration traps, end to end
item.dc:creator: Priya Nair
item.description: OpenAI's GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol shipped on November 17 with apply_patch and shell as first-class Responses API tools. This tutorial builds a complete coding agent on them — file edits, test runs, structured reports, and cost control — with every request verified against the official docs.

item.title: Blue TTS v3 promises 50x real-time speech on a plain CPU — its own repo’s numbers top out at 38x
item.dc:creator: Priya Nair
item.description: Blue TTS v3 is a 388 MB open-source voice that runs locally in seven languages — but the 50x real-time claim in its launch post outruns every number in the project’s own speed table, and Reddit spent the day checking the math.

item.title: Claude turned one prompt into Hearthly, a smart-home site that becomes a horror movie as you scroll
item.dc:creator: Sofia Almeida
item.description: A Reddit user asked Claude to build a generic marketing website that gets weirder the further you scroll. The result — “Hearthly, the smart home that cares” — went from cozy to chilling in a day, passing 1,600 upvotes as readers discovered its fake camera feed and its “Forever” plan you can never cancel.

item.title: Reddit says Google just proved recursive self-improvement. The paper says something narrower.
item.dc:creator: Priya Nair
item.description: A Google paper on self-improving agent harnesses is going viral as proof that AI can now improve itself. The paper is real — but the improvement is to the harness, not the model, and the top comments on Reddit are the ones saying so.

item.title: Steer any LLM without training: hands-on with Heretic, the 41,000-star model modifier
item.dc:creator: Sofia Almeida
item.description: Heretic modifies LLMs without training — refusal suppression, slop and sycophancy removal via a scored search over weight edits. This tutorial installs 2.1.0, runs it on Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct on CPU, and takes refusals from 15/20 to 0/20, with every command verified.

item.title: UK MPs call for an AI Safety and Security Bill — and a regulator with the power to halt risky models
item.dc:creator: Priya Nair
item.description: Parliament’s Business, Innovation, Science and Trade Committee says Britain’s voluntary approach to AI safety has run out of road. Its report calls for a statutory regulator that can halt training, block deployments and suspend services — and wants the law passed in the next session.

item.title: A 17 MB self-hosted Netflix built with Claude Code passed 1,500 GitHub stars in nine days
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: HolyArrs squeezes six home-media apps into a single 16 MB download built with Claude Code — and in nine days it has passed 1,500 GitHub stars and 24,000 Docker pulls. It does not replace Plex, and its developer is the first to say it is still beta.

item.title: RUMOR: Gemini 4 Neon pricing leaks into Google Cloud billing catalog as Google stays silent
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: Pricing for an unannounced Gemini 4 Neon model has appeared in Google Cloud's billing catalog at $3 in and $15 out per million tokens — but Google has said nothing, and the model can’t be called yet.

item.title: Klarna’s AI assistant does your errands: shopping, returns and restaurant bookings over WhatsApp and iMessage
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: Klarna’s new AI assistant books tables, buys gifts, chases returns and drafts your emails — from inside WhatsApp and iMessage. It’s live for a small group of early users, with a waitlist now open.

item.title: Build a multi-agent research team with Google's ADK: researcher, writer, and guardrails, end to end
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: Google's Agent Development Kit turns multi-agent systems into plain Python: a coordinator, a researcher with Google Search, a writer, a save tool with a guardrail, and an eval that pins the behaviour. This tutorial builds the whole team — every command verified against ADK 2.14.
